title: Understand a waiting update
summary: A new worker may wait while the old one still controls open pages.
introduction: A new worker may wait while the old one still controls open pages. Your task: Inspect active and waiting workers after changing sw.js.
learningObjectives: Inspect active and waiting workers after changing sw.js.
Explain the example for understand a waiting update

blocks.text: A new worker may wait while the old one still controls open pages. This avoids mixing a new app version with an old page halfway through a task.

These examples belong in separate files on your own HTTPS or localhost site. Service workers need that trusted origin and cannot run in this site's sandbox. Use browser developer tools to inspect them.

blocks.title: Understand a waiting update

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `waiting` refers to an installed worker that has not yet replaced the active worker for existing pages.

blocks.text: The console shows the active worker and, when present, a waiting version. The values depend on the current installation state.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Do not force an update and reload in the middle of unsaved work. Offer a clear update action when needed.
